definition: The generation effect is the idea that people may perform better later when they first produce their own response, idea, or position instead of directly adopting one supplied by a tool or other source. In this packet, it is mentioned as a possible explanation for why a self-generation-first workflow led to better later unaided reasoning than a direct-adoption workflow, but no mechanism was established.

reasons: The definition’s first sentence states a general claim (“people may perform better later”) that is not clearly supported by the packet as written; the packet describes that dependent users reasoned worse than a no-AI baseline, while autonomous users did not fall below that baseline (not demonstrated as “better later”).

The packet does not provide a concise, standalone definition of “generation effect” as a term; it only says “A generation-effect account is consistent with the pattern” and that the design cannot establish a mechanism, so the requested sense/meaning is not sufficiently grounded in the packet.

The second sentence’s claim (“no mechanism was established”) is supported, but because the first sentence contains an unsupported generalization about improved later performance, the overall definition is not defensible against the packet.
